newsitem.title: NEW ZEALAND: Here comes the bride...there goes the groom.
newsitem.headline: Here comes the bride...there goes the groom.

text.p: A groom who bolted while making his marriage vows had to be rescued by police when his irate bride and prospective mother-in-law chased him into the street, the New Zealand Press Association (NZPA) reported on Friday.
Overcome by second thoughts as he was about to tie the knot, the groom fled the downtown Auckland registry office. Incensed, the bride and her mother promptly gave chase.
A potential confrontation was avoided when a passing police patrol car spotted a sprinting man and stopped to see if he needed help.
"He leapt into the back and said; 'Quick, drive'," said Detective Senior Sergeant Tony Wakelin.
The patrol car sped off, leaving the two women in its wake, and took the distraught groom back to his family.
NZPA said the bride's family apparently insisted on marriage when they learned she was pregnant.
Police would not comment on the likelihood of a reconciliation, saying they hoped to take no further part in the couple's nuptials.
